meta.date: ~600 BC (in vision, from the valley of Lemuel)

world_behind.title: Mountains are where seers are taken
world_behind.text: Moses on Sinai, Ezekiel set upon a very high mountain for his temple vision, John carried to a great high mountain for his (Rev. 21:10): the setting is the old grammar of large revelation. Nephi notes that he had never seen this mountain and never set foot on it — the geography itself is given, not climbed.

world_behind.title: Nazareth, named early
world_behind.text: The vision picks out "the city of Nazareth" (v. 13), a small Galilean village with no role in Israel's scriptures, six centuries before the events that made it famous. The record's habit of specific place-names (Bethabara in ch. 10, Nazareth here) puts its prophecy at documentary risk on purpose.

cites.quote: the city of Nazareth

spans.text: the city of Nazareth

world_behind.title: A virgin mother was already Israel's hope
world_behind.text: Isaiah's sign of the virgin with child (Isa. 7:14) sat on the brass plates the family carried. What the vision adds is portraiture: the city, the fairness, the child in her arms — the sign turned into a scene.

world_behind.title: The dove at the river
world_behind.text: The vision's baptism matches the Gospel accounts to the detail of the Spirit's descending form (Matt. 3:16). For Lehi's family, washing was ritual; a heavens-open baptism with the Spirit abiding was new; prophecy again at the resolution of an eyewitness.

world_behind.title: A strange way to die
world_behind.text: "lifted up upon the cross" (v. 33) describes an execution foreign to Israel's law, which stoned its condemned. The vision shows a Roman death centuries before Rome ruled anything east of Italy, and the record simply reports it, letting the oddity stand.

cites.quote: lifted up upon the cross

spans.text: lifted up upon the cross

world_behind.title: Hosanna was liturgy
world_behind.text: The Spirit's cry (v. 6) uses the old festival shout, save now, from the procession psalms (Ps. 118:25). Crowds would one day cry it at the Messiah himself (Matt. 21:9). In the vision it is heaven's own word, shouted over one believing man.

words.text: The launch posture: "as I sat pondering in mine heart I was caught away" (v. 1). Pondering is weighing: slow, seated, deliberate thought, and the record makes it the runway of the whole vision. Nephi is not fasting on the mountain or pleading in the dark; he is sitting with his father's words, turning them, when the Spirit takes him.

cites.quote: as I sat pondering in mine heart I was caught away

spans.text: as I sat pondering in mine heart I was caught away

words.text: The old shout of salvation, and its placement here is the surprise: the Spirit himself cries it — not over the vision about to be given but over the faith that preceded it, "blessed art thou, Nephi, because thou believest" (v. 6). Heaven celebrates belief before it rewards it.

cites.quote: blessed art thou, Nephi, because thou believest

spans.text: blessed art thou, Nephi, because thou believest

words.text: The tree's meaning is promised as an event: "thou shalt also behold a man descending out of heaven" (v. 7). The sign is not attached to the symbol; the sign is a person. The whole chapter's method sits inside this word: its interpretations are appearances, and to understand is to witness.

cites.quote: thou shalt also behold a man descending out of heaven

spans.text: thou shalt also behold a man descending out of heaven

words.text: The Holy Ghost did not visit the baptized Lamb but came down and "abide upon him in the form of a dove" (v. 27): settled, stayed, made a dwelling. The verb quietly distinguishes the Messiah's endowment from every fleeting inspiration, and gives the reader a word for what to want.

cites.quote: abide upon him in the form of a dove

spans.text: abide upon him in the form of a dove

phrases.text: The vision opens with a question and repeats it (v. 10). Heaven's interview method assumes the seer must name his want before receiving it, twice. Desire, in this record's doctrine of revelation, is not a mood that happens to a man; it is a faculty he is asked to aim.

The vision's working verb, issued again and again (v. 8, 12, 19, 24, 26, 30–32). Nephi's part is commanded attention; the content is supplied. The rhythm teaches what seership is in this record, obedient looking, and what it is not: imagination.

To condescend is to descend-with, rank voluntarily coming down to stand with the low; the record's word for the incarnation is a word about direction. It is asked as a question (v. 16), then issued as a command: "Look and behold the condescension of God" (v. 26). The doubling splits the doctrine in two: the condescension of the Father giving a Son to flesh, and the condescension of the Son walking into rejection and death. The chapter is built between those two uses.

cites.quote: Look and behold the condescension of God

spans.text: Look and behold the condescension of God

phrases.text: Planted at 1 Ne. 10:10, the title becomes the vision's refrain here, the angel's name for Christ in nearly every frame. The choice is deliberate doctrine: ministry, healing, and judgment are all shown under a sacrificial title, so the reader never sees the Messiah without seeing where his story goes.

Nephi's superlative for the tree, and the angel immediately adds a second: "the most joyous to the soul" (v. 23). Desirable is the seeker's word; joyous is the taster's. Between the two, the record prices the love of God from both sides of receiving it.

cites.quote: the most joyous to the soul

spans.text: the most joyous to the soul

phrases.text: The witness formula, delivered under commission (v. 7 promised Nephi would "bear record that it is the Son of God" (v. 7)). Seeing in this chapter is legal work: what is beheld must be attested. The formula returns at the building's fall (v. 36), bracketing the vision's climax in testimony language.

cites.quote: bear record that it is the Son of God

spans.text: bear record that it is the Son of God

verses.label: v. 1
verses.title: The runway
verses.text: Desire, belief, pondering, then the mountain. The verse is 1 Nephi 10:17–19 enacted: the doctrine that the vision gift answers diligent seeking is tested on its own author, sitting still, thinking hard, believing "that the Lord was able to make them known" (v. 1).

cites.quote: that the Lord was able to make them known

spans.text: that the Lord was able to make them known

verses.label: v. 2–7
verses.title: The interview
verses.text: Before anything is shown, Nephi is asked what he wants and whether he believes. His answer earns a Hosanna and a commission: he will see the tree, then see "a man descending out of heaven" (v. 7), and must bear record. The vision's terms are set as a covenant before its first image.

cites.quote: a man descending out of heaven

spans.text: a man descending out of heaven

verses.label: v. 8–12
verses.title: The tree, and the guide's exit
verses.text: The tree exceeds even his father's telling, whiteness beyond "the whiteness of the driven snow" (v. 8). But at the question of meaning, the Spirit vanishes mid-conversation, and an angel takes the tour. Even the machinery of the vision teaches: interpretation is a different errand from sight, with its own escort.

cites.quote: the whiteness of the driven snow

spans.text: the whiteness of the driven snow

verses.label: v. 13–20
verses.title: The answer is a mother
verses.text: Asked if he knows the condescension of God, Nephi gives the record's most quoted honest answer: "I know that he loveth his children; nevertheless, I do not know the meaning of all things" (v. 17). The angel's response is not a definition but a scene: Nazareth, a virgin, and then "the virgin again, bearing a child in her arms" (v. 20). The vision defines love by showing what love did.

cites.quote: I know that he loveth his children; nevertheless, I do not know the meaning of all things

spans.text: I know that he loveth his children; nevertheless, I do not know the meaning of all things

cites.quote: the virgin again, bearing a child in her arms

spans.text: the virgin again, bearing a child in her arms

verses.label: v. 21–25
verses.title: The symbols keyed
verses.text: In five verses the dream's code unlocks: the tree is "the love of God" (v. 22), the rod is "the word of God" (v. 25), the waters are that same love again. Every key points at the child of verse 20; the interpretation of the whole dream turns out to be one person.

cites.quote: the love of God

spans.text: the love of God

cites.quote: the word of God

spans.text: the word of God

verses.label: v. 26–33
verses.title: Condescension, part two
verses.text: The second Look-command opens the ministry: baptism, the abiding dove, healing multitudes, the Twelve, and then the turn: "the Son of the everlasting God was judged of the world" (v. 32), lifted up, "slain for the sins of the world" (v. 33). The vision never softens the sequence; the same God who came down keeps descending, all the way through a cross.

cites.quote: the Son of the everlasting God was judged of the world

spans.text: the Son of the everlasting God was judged of the world

cites.quote: slain for the sins of the world

spans.text: slain for the sins of the world

verses.label: v. 34–36
verses.title: The building falls
verses.text: The world gathers against the Lamb's apostles, is housed in the dream's spacious building, named "the pride of the world" (v. 36), and dropped: "the fall thereof was exceedingly great" (v. 36). The dream's last unexplained symbol receives both its meaning and its ending, and the chapter closes on the wreckage.

cites.quote: the pride of the world

spans.text: the pride of the world

cites.quote: the fall thereof was exceedingly great

spans.text: the fall thereof was exceedingly great

chapter.title: The asking doctrine, run live
chapter.text: Chapter 10 claimed the vision gift belongs to every diligent seeker; this chapter is the claim's first trial: desire named, belief confessed, and the heavens opened to a young man who was not the prophet of his family. The unit's controlled experiment has its positive result.

chapter.title: Meaning is given by pointing
chapter.text: Asked what the tree means, the vision shows a person; asked about condescension, it shows a baptism and a cross. The record's teaching method peaks here — the answer the record gives to every "what does it mean?" is finally "look at him."

chapter.title: An honest witness's credentials
chapter.text: Nephi's "I do not know the meaning of all things" (v. 17) sits beside his absolute "I know that he loveth his children" (v. 17): the record's model of testimony: fixed certainty at the center, confessed ignorance at the edges, and no shame about either.

cites.quote: I do not know the meaning of all things

spans.text: I do not know the meaning of all things

cites.quote: I know that he loveth his children

spans.text: I know that he loveth his children

chapter.title: The vision sets the record's vocabulary
chapter.text: The angel's consistent naming does long-term work: from this chapter forward, "the Lamb" is how the vision chapters say Christ (chs. 12–14 run on the title), and the record's later writers inherit the usage. One conversation on a mountain fixed the book's way of speaking about its central figure.

chapter.title: Witness is the vision's product
chapter.text: Commissioned at verse 7, delivered at verses 32 and 36, the bear-record formula turns private sight into public testimony. The chapter exists because the commission was kept — the reader is holding the record it commanded.

chapter.title: The dream keyed, with mirrors home
chapter.text: Tree, rod, waters, and building each receive their meaning here, and each key clicks back into chapter 8's lock. Read as a pair, the chapters teach the unit's method: symbols are given to families, and interpretations to seekers.

chapter.title: The fall is a promise, not a threat
chapter.text: The building's collapse ends the chapter as prophecy already witnessed: pride's destruction is shown as accomplished fact inside the vision. The record's polemic against the world's wisdom starts from its ending, which it has already seen.

applications.title: Build a pondering seat
applications.text: The vision found Nephi sitting still with his father's words. Give your seeking the same runway: a fixed place and unhurried time where the last thing read gets weighed, not just finished. Caught-away moments in this record favor the seated.

applications.title: Answer the interview question
applications.text: "What desirest thou?" assumes you can say. Write your answer in one sentence, the specific spiritual thing you want to see, know, or receive, and pray that sentence instead of your usual circumference.

applications.title: Hold the two knowings
applications.text: Practice Nephi's balance out loud: one sentence of certainty (he loves his children) and one of honest limit (I don't know the meaning of this). Use the pair the next time a hard question comes at your faith — it is sturdier than pretended completeness in either direction.

applications.title: Look when told to look
applications.text: The vision's gift traveled entirely through commanded attention. Treat the promptings toward attention the same way (the verse to reread, the person to notice, the meeting to actually hear) as Look-commands, and obey a few this week deliberately.

applications.title: Name your Lamb-frames
applications.text: The vision would not show ministry without the cross in the title. When you tell the story of your blessings, keep the Redeemer's name on the frames, not "things worked out" but who worked them, and watch what the renaming does to gratitude.

applications.title: Bear the record soon
applications.text: Sight decays into memory, and memory into impression. Whatever you have actually seen God do, convert it to testimony while it is still sight: written, spoken, dated. Nephi's vision reached you because he filed it.

questions.text: Where and when do I ponder — and if nowhere, what fills the seat where a vision's runway would go?
Could I state my deepest current spiritual desire in one plain sentence, and when did I last pray it that plainly?
Whose words do I believe the way Nephi believed Lehi's — and does my believing show in what I then do?
What is my honest "I do not know" right now, and is it resting beside a firm "I know," or trying to replace it?
If I had to show someone the love of God rather than define it, where would I point first?
When the crowd's mood turns against what I heard gladly, do I stay gathered to hear, or drift with the casting-out?
Which spacious structure has my scorn in it, and what does this chapter say its foundation is?
